rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 and 3 - authors report their own governance evaluation with the OECD indicator tool and a questionnaire-based perception analysis of 71 workshop participants in three pilot areas. Q2: Section 2.1 and Figs 3-4 - the WATERMED platform's first layer integrates IoT sensors, satellite imagery, open sources, piezometers and governance indicators and delivers services to farmers, irrigation communities and managers; Section 3.2.1-3.2.3 - 94% of Turkish, 75% of Spanish and 83% of Algerian respondents said interaction with the platform's governance tool helped them learn and they are interested in using it in future; Section 3.1 states the platform was introduced and tested in the three basins. Q5: Sections 3.1.1-3.1.3 and 3.2.1-3.2.3 report separate results for Konya (Turkiye), Jucar-Vinalopo (Spain) and Upper Cheliff (Algeria). Q6: Section 2.2 and 3.1 - the platform and evaluation were applied at basin/sub-basin and irrigation-community scale, not at plot scale. Q7: Abstract and Sections 3.1.1-3.1.3 - from the perception results the authors state that end users require technical and financial support, that adoption needs time, dedication and training of farmers and authorities, and that investment costs and funding restrictions must be addressed.
rows.notes: The passage is largely descriptive (platforms are welcome and implemented). The study supports it in that it describes implementation of a platform integrating satellite imagery, sensors and piezometers and reports stakeholder self-reported acceptance; however the perception questionnaire concerns mainly the water governance evaluation tool and the platform as a whole, not satellite/remote-sensing services specifically, and 'social cohesion' is only indirectly addressed via learning/engagement items. Evidence is all stakeholder self-report (workshops, questionnaire, self-completed OECD indicators) so no independent method (Q3). No limitation of the sample (71 participants, 77% with university degree) or method is stated as a limitation; only percentages reported, no dispersion.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a platform-development and stakeholder-perception paper; the remote-sensing component is one input layer of the platform and is not evaluated separately.
